editorial:
Nick Gant is a young psychic hiding in Hong Kong after Division killed his father, and he is not exactly living his best life. When a teenage clairvoyant named Cassie shows up with a dangerous plan, Nick gets pulled into a hunt for a missing girl and a stolen suitcase that could change everything. The movie throws you into a world of mind readers, movers, and shady government agents, so it feels like a comic book come to life. The city setting gives it a gritty, colorful energy, and the story moves fast enough to keep you guessing. You do not need to know every psychic rule right away; the film explains things as it goes, which makes it easy to follow even when the plot gets twisty.

The action is the main draw, with telekinetic fights, chase scenes, and clever psychic tricks that keep the energy high. Chris Evans brings charm and frustration to Nick, while Dakota Fanning gives Cassie a sharp, funny edge that makes their team-up work. The movie is not perfect: some characters feel underused, and the story can get crowded with powers and factions. Still, if you enjoy stylish sci-fi with a rebellious streak, this is a fun ride. Watch it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Nick and Cassie outsmart Division by using a plan Cassie predicted but kept hidden. Nick appears to be captured and injected with a dangerous drug, but it is part of the trick. The missing girl, Kira, escapes with the suitcase, and Division’s leader is left chasing the wrong trail. Nick and Cassie reunite, having beaten the agency for now. The twist is that Cassie’s vision of a bad future was actually a setup to make Division believe they had won, leaving the heroes free to continue fighting.
